items.title: What does Terminal actually do?

content.text: Terminal is an AI-native Yard Operating System
TM
(YOS
TM
) that uses computer vision to automate yard execution from gate to dock. It replaces manual logs with a system that proactively decides and executes the next best move in real-time.

items.title: How is this different from a traditional Yard Management System (YMS)?

content.text: Traditional YMS are "digital clipboards" that record what already happened; Terminal is an
operating
system that sees what is happening now and orchestrates what needs to happen next in the yard.

items.title: What is "Agentic AI" in the context of the yard?

content.text: It acts as a 24/7 autonomous supervisor that handles exceptions and reprioritizes tasks based on real-time conditions, ensuring the most critical moves happen first (e.g. how to prepare and reallocate resources for a late appointment)

items.title: How accurate is the data captured by your system?

content.text: Our proprietary computer vision stack delivers 50% or more improvement in data accuracy vs. manual operations, virtually eliminating the human error and "lost assets" common with manual entry.

items.title: Can we manage multiple sites from a single login?

content.text: Yes; Terminal provides a "Global Control Tower" view, allowing you to compare KPIs, dwell times, and performance across all facilities in your network in one place.

items.title: How is Terminal priced?

content.text: Terminal is priced as a competitive annual, all-inclusive as-a-service model for all hardware, support, and services. Deployments can vary and are charged as a separate up-front fee.

items.title: What kind of ROI can I expect?

content.text: Most customers see a 4x+ ROI within the first year and achieve a full payback in less than 5 months through labor savings and faster throughput.

items.title: How does Terminal reduce carrier and facility costs?

content.text: We reduce labor costs by automating routine yard tasks, reduce driver detention fees by improving gate processing times, faster responsiveness at the dock, and maximum visibility to all asset inventory in the yard.

items.title: Can Terminal help with regulatory compliance?

content.text: Yes; our Indirect Source Rule (ISR) feature automates compliance by generating audit-ready data for regulations like Rule 2305.

items.title: Who is Terminal best suited for?

content.text: Highly modular, Terminal is built for both mid-market and enterprise 3PLs, retailers, and manufacturers managing complex, medium- to high-volume multi-yard networks that want to scale without adding headcount.

items.title: Is Terminal a stable long-term partner?

content.text: Founded in 2023 and backed by 8VC and four of the top 10 U.S. logistics firms (including Prologis and Ryder), Terminal offers deep financial and strategic stability.

items.title: How fast can we go live?

content.text: Gate automation can be live in as little as 5 days, with full yard orchestration typically completed in 45 days.

items.title: Does Terminal integrate with my existing WMS/TMS?

content.text: Yes; we offer seamless, event-driven integration with major platforms like Manhattan, SAP, Blue Yonder, FourKites, and project44.

items.title: Do I need to buy expensive proprietary cameras?

content.text: No; Terminal is hardware-agnostic and can often leverage your existing IP cameras, or you can use our plug-and-play "Terminal in a Camera" bundles.

items.title: Is the platform modular or "all-or-nothing"?

content.text: The system is highly configurable; you can start with a single use case, like Gate Acceleration, and expand into full yard orchestration over time.

items.title: What happens if our site’s internet goes down?

content.text: Terminal is designed with local resilience; mission-critical tasks continue to buffer locally and sync to the cloud once connectivity is restored.

items.title: How does Terminal protect my data?

content.text: We use a zero-trust security model with industry-standard encryption and are currently in the process of achieving SOC-2 compliance.

items.title: How do drivers and yard spotters interact with the system?

content.text: Terminal is browser-based (no app to download). Drivers can use their personal mobile devices, while spotters and dock workers can be outfitted with any browser-enabled mobile device approved by the operator.

items.title: How does this change the role of my yard office staff?

content.text: Staff shift from manual data entry to "exception management," only intervening when the AI flags a specific issue that requires human judgment.

items.title: Will implementation disrupt my current operations?

content.text: No; our deployment model requires little operational downtime and carries a very low IT lift for your team.

items.title: What kind of support and training do you provide?

content.text: We provide "White-Glove" on-site training for all shifts, 24/7 live technical support, and a dedicated hypercare period post-launch.

items.title: What is your system availability guarantee?

content.text: As long as yard internet is running, Terminal runs at a 99.9% uptime for all mission-critical workflows to ensure your yard operations never stop.

FAQs
Here are the most common questions teams have before getting started with Terminal.

items.title: Resistance to operational change

content.text: Yards traditionally rely on manual processes and are resistant to change. This ingrained culture makes it difficult to introduce new technology. Terminal's approach provides a strong ROI case to business leaders, making the financial benefits of change compelling, while its simple, turnkey deployment and managed infrastructure reduce the friction of adoption.

items.title: Worker resistance to automation

content.text: Workers worry about losing their jobs to new technology. This fear can lead to resistance from frontline staff and create a negative environment for adoption. Terminal uses a human-in-the-loop onboarding process that redefines roles, allowing staff to be redeployed to higher-value tasks, and provides ongoing support, which alleviates job security fears.

items.title: Skepticism from failed pilots

content.text: Customers are wary of new solutions due to past failures with other vendors. This long memory of past disappointments makes them cautious about investing again. Terminal builds trust with referenceable customers and proven performance, demonstrating a faster time-to-value (5 days vs. competitors' 5+ months) and lower deployment costs through rapid, successful results.

items.title: Fear of workflow disruption

content.text: Operators are afraid that new technology will break their existing, established, and profitable processes. This fear of risk outweighs the upside benefits for many companies. Terminal’s simple, turnkey deployment model and modular, on/off capability minimize this risk, allowing customers to start small and integrate the solution without a complete overhaul of their operations.

items.title: Cybersecurity and privacy risks

content.text: New interconnected yard systems introduce new vulnerabilities and data management risks. Companies with legacy systems or fragmented operations are especially vulnerable to these threats. As a fully managed solution with a unified, cloud-based platform, Terminal provides a secure, single-source system that is inherently more secure than managing a fragmented collection of different legacy tools.

items.title: Complex system integration challenges

content.text: New technology often doesn't fit with a customer's legacy software ecosystem. This creates a risk of operational disruption and requires significant resources to build custom integrations. Terminal's modular, API-based platform is designed for seamless integration, easily connecting with existing business systems both upstream and downstream.

items.title: Lack of on-site IT infrastructure

content.text: Yards often lack reliable power, lighting, or internet access. This poor infrastructure makes it difficult to deploy and operate new technology. Terminal's solution includes a fully managed infrastructure that can bundle power, network, lighting, and cameras into a single, affordable annual fee.

items.title: Limited technical staff

content.text: Operators that do not have the in-house expertise to set up and maintain complex technology struggle to manage deployments and troubleshoot issues. Terminal provides a turnkey deployment and training model with robust delivery and support processes, ensuring a smooth and hands-off implementation.

items.title: Fragmented yard technology market

content.text: The market is crowded with old technology and no unified solutions. This forces customers to evaluate numerous point solutions that don't integrate well. Terminal builds an all-in-one solution that avoids the need for multiple, inadequate products that are costly and fail to deliver real ROI.

items.title: Fragmented technology across yards

content.text: Different yards often use different, inconsistent tools. This lack of standardization leads to poor data quality and makes it difficult to manage a portfolio of yards. Terminal provides a unified, AI-driven "
OS for the Yard
" that integrates with legacy systems and TMS/WMS, ensuring consistency across a customer's entire operation.

items.title: Unreliable legacy tagging technology

content.text: Physical tags and signals like RFID, GPS, and IoT often fail in real-world yard environments. These technologies can have accuracy issues, signal interference, or require complex maintenance. Terminal’s computer vision accurately identifies assets visually without relying on physical tags or signals, making it more scalable, less invasive, and proven accurate in deployments and a more feasible solution for yard with different load carriers.

items.title: Desire to find the perfect solution

content.text: Operators often get bogged down by the desire for a perfect, customized solution from the start. This pursuit of a comprehensive system leads to an endless scope of work and project failure before anything can be implemented. Terminal's turnkey and simple deployment model, which delivers value in as little as 5 days, is built to counteract this, providing tangible results and a clear path to expansion without getting lost in endless customization.

items.title: High cost and ROI uncertainty

content.text: Technology is often seen as too expensive with an unclear return on investment. Customers worry that the high installation costs and thin margins of yard operations won't justify the expense. Terminal offers affordable, turnkey, and simple bundled pricing with an all-in-one investment option and modular capabilities that allow customers to scale their investment and see a clear, fast return.

items.title: Costly regulatory compliance burdens

content.text: Meeting local regulatory requirements, such as ISR in Southern California, is a time-consuming and expensive process. Manual compliance is also prone to error and can lead to costly fines. Terminal’s ISR Compliance solution provides full automation via computer vision, which drastically reduces the risk of fines and simplifies the entire compliance process.

items.title: Flawed ROI metrics and focus

content.text: Customers have a narrow view of ROI, often focusing only on how many people they can displace. This approach ignores other significant costs, such as driver detention and wasted capacity. Terminal's strong ROI case highlights value beyond labor, including faster time-to-value, reductions in driver detention fees, and increased asset utilization, which are more compelling to executive-level buyers.

items.title: Inefficient manual gate processes

content.text: Manual, error-prone gate check-in/out processes cause delays and inefficiency. These issues result in increased driver wait times and administrative errors. Terminal enables Gate Acceleration with computer vision (CV) and tablet automation, reducing truck dwell time from 5-10 minutes to less than 5 minutes.

items.title: The yard black hole

content.text: The yard is often seen as an unstructured and chaotic "black hole" within the supply chain. This perception causes the area to be overlooked in digital transformation efforts, even as other parts of the supply chain become more digitized. Terminal's unified platform directly addresses this problem by bringing a high degree of structure, automation, and real-time visibility to the yard, making it a visible and manageable part of the supply chain for the first time.

items.title: Absence of unified industry standards

content.text: There is a lack of standardized protocols and data formats for yard technology. This makes it challenging to integrate solutions with different systems and partners. Terminal's API-driven "OS for the Yard" acts as a unifying layer, built to integrate seamlessly with various legacy systems and partner platforms, effectively creating a single standard for the customer.

items.title: Poor data quality and capture

content.text: Data is often messy, unreliable, or captured inconsistently across yard operations. This makes it difficult to make data-driven decisions and identify opportunities for improvement. Terminal's
CV and AI technology
create a unified platform and data lake, as computer vision is the most efficient and accurate method for yard data capture, accommodating unstructured data and providing high-quality information.

items.title: Lack of real-time visibility

content.text: Finding trailers and conducting manual asset inventory is time-consuming and inefficient. This lack of visibility leads to wasted labor hours and lost capacity. Terminal's Cloud Capture & Asset Inventory Solution, powered by computer vision and a cloud ML pipeline, indexes asset data in real-time and automates inventory validation in just 20–30 minutes per day versus the traditional 4–6 hours.
The Most Common
Technology Hurdles in the Yard
Here are the most common hurdles to technology adoption in the yard. Choose the one that is holding you back to see how Terminal can help.

items.title: What does Terminal do for a single yard?

content.text: Terminal is an AI-native Yard Operating System
TM
(YOS
TM
) that uses computer vision to to automate check-in, locate every trailer, and direct moves — for one yard or many. You get the same automation the big operators run, sized to your site.

items.title: Do I need to tag my trailers or install RFID?

content.text: No. Terminal reads trucks and trailers with computer vision, so there's nothing to tag, scan, or maintain.

items.title: How is this different from the spreadsheet or whiteboard I use now?

content.text: A spreadsheet records what someone remembered to type; Terminal sees what's actually happening in your yard right now and acts on it. It's the difference between a logbook and a live system.

items.title: Do I need an IT team to run it?

content.text: No. It's cloud-based with minimal IT lift, no servers to buy and no infrastructure to manage.

items.title: Does the AI really work on a smaller yard?

content.text: Yes. The computer vision delivers the same accuracy whether you run 50 moves a day or 500,  a smaller operation just needs fewer cameras.

items.title: Isn't a whole operating system overkill for one or two yards?

content.text: Not the way Terminal is built. You start with the single capability you need, like the gate, and add more only when it pays off. You're never buying a platform you won't use.

items.title: What kind of ROI can I expect?

content.text: Most customers see a 4x+ ROI within the first year and achieve a full payback in less than 5 months through labor savings and faster throughput.

items.title: Will I actually see ROI at my size?

content.text: Yes. Detention, lost trailers, and wasted spotter time cost you on a small yard too, and customers typically see measurable returns within about five months.

items.title: Is there a big upfront cost?

content.text: No. Pricing is all-inclusive and service-based with no large capital outlay, built for lean yard budgets. There may be a small up-front deployment fee depending on the complexity of your operation and customization required.

items.title: How small can I start?

content.text: As small as one capability at one site, and you scale up modules and add yards entirely on your own timeline.

items.title: What's the catch with starting small?

content.text: There isn't one. Modular by design means you run only what you need, and adding the rest later takes days, not a re-implementation.

items.title: How long until I'm up and running?

content.text: A basic deployment can be live in as little as five days, and the Terminal-in-a-Camera™ kit installs in hours, no long IT project.

items.title: Does Terminal integrate with my existing WMS/TMS?

content.text: Yes; we offer seamless, event-driven integration with major platforms like Manhattan, SAP, Blue Yonder, FourKites, and project44.

items.title: Do I need to install new infrastructure?

content.text: No. There are no on-premise servers and no major site modifications; the camera kit and the cloud do the work. We can even use existing cameras depending on their placement.

items.title: How much of my team's time will this take?

content.text: Hours. Setup is low-touch on your side, and training is hands-on and quick for gate, yard, and office staff.

items.title: What does getting started actually look like?

content.text: Terminal follows a simple crawl-walk-run path: start with core features, then layer in automation as you're comfortable, rather than flipping a switch on everything at once.

items.title: How does Terminal protect my data?

content.text: We use a zero-trust security model with industry-standard encryption and are currently in the process of achieving SOC-2 compliance.

items.title: Can I start with just the gate, or just one piece?

content.text: Yes. You can run a single module (gate, visibility, or security) and it works on its own from day one.

items.title: Can I run my gate unmanned?

content.text: Yes. Terminal can run the gate fully unmanned, manned, or a mix. Your choice, per site.

items.title: Do my drivers and spotters need special devices?

content.text: No special hardware required. Spotters, drivers, and dock workers use a simple browser-based application.

items.title: How about reporting?

content.text: Data from one site, and all sites, are available in through a single browser-based portal. Check your gates, lot, dock activity today and see trends over time.

items.title: What happens when I add a second or third yard later?

content.text: All yards connect into one view automatically, so adding a site is an expansion of what you already know, not a new project.

items.title: Do I need to tag my trailers?

content.text: No. Terminal locates assets with computer vision, so there's nothing to tag, issue, or replace.

items.title: How current is the yard map?

content.text: Continuously updated, not a once-a-shift snapshot.

items.title: Can I see multiple yards in one place?

content.text: Yes. Sites roll up into a single network view.

items.title: Will this fix my detention disputes?

content.text: With accurate, timestamped locations managers know exactly when a trailer enters the gate and how long it sits before reaching the dock. This prevents trailers from sitting unlocated and racking up carrier penalties.
